title: Thousands of Hezbollah pagers explode across Lebanon
body:
On 17 September 2024, beginning around 15:30 local time and lasting about an hour, pagers used by Hezbollah members exploded across Lebanon. Al Jazeera reported at the time of publication that at least nine people had been killed and 2,750 wounded, according to security services and the Lebanese health minister. Health Minister Firass Abiad said more than 200 of the wounded were in critical condition, with injuries mostly to the face, hands and stomach.

Those killed included an eight-year-old girl and Mohammad Mahdi Ammar, son of Hezbollah member of parliament Ali Ammar, and Hezbollah confirmed that two of its fighters had died. Mojtaba Amani, Iran's ambassador to Lebanon, was injured. A later Al Jazeera report said about 4,000 pagers exploded, killing 12 people and injuring nearly 3,000.

Hezbollah said it held "the Israeli enemy fully responsible" and warned that Israel would receive "just punishment." Lebanese Information Minister Ziad Makary also condemned the attack. Israel did not comment at the time. How the pagers exploded was initially unclear, with speculation including a hacked radio network, tampering in the supply chain, or a battery overheating through a malicious trigger. The blasts were followed the next day by a second wave of explosions in walkie-talkies and other devices, and by Israel's strike that killed Hassan Nasrallah on 27 September 2024.
